a.summary: This commit added 8 javadoc lines to `SolanaRpcClient.java` above two accepted mutants but did not re-tag their rows, so `client-accepted.csv` now carries the exact line-drift defect D5 was filed to close.
a.failure_scenario: Run `pitestClient` on the post-commit tree. PIT reports the two accepted `SolanaRpcClient.sendTransaction` conditional mutants at source lines 1033 and 1042, while the baseline rows claim 1034 and 1025. Both rows fail the row-level line match, so the hardening plugin emits a permanent line-drift advisory (sava-build/HARDENING.md:1293-1296, 1356) that no amount of re-running clears — the same permanent advisory D5 described. A maintainer triaging the advisory and following `# line 1025` lands on `: sendTransaction(base64SignedTx, maxRetries);`, the else-arm of a *different* overload's ternary, not the guard the `# killed retained` acceptance argues about.

b.summary: This commit's own +8-line javadoc insertion into SolanaRpcClient.java invalidated two `# line` tags in client-accepted.csv that were not retagged, reintroducing the exact line-drift advisory the commit set out to clear — and both stale numbers now land inside a different `sendTransaction` overload.
b.failure_scenario: Run `pitestClient` (or `BaselineRetag`) on the post-commit tree. PIT reports the `RemoveConditionalMutator_EQUAL_ELSE` mutant on `SolanaRpcClient.sendTransaction` at line 1042 and the `EQUAL_IF` sibling at 1033, while the baseline records 1034 and 1025 -> a line-drift advisory on two rows. AGENTS.md:126-127 then requires a reviewer to treat each advisory as a possible mutant swap; the reviewer opens SolanaRpcClient.java:1034, lands on `? sendTransactionSkipPreflight(preflightCommitment, base64SignedTx)` inside the three-argument `sendTransaction(Commitment, String, boolean)` overload, and 1025 lands inside `sendTransaction(String, int)` — two different, identically-shaped ternaries — so the written `# killed retained` argument appears to fit code it was never written about.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
